exercises.name: Bodyweight squat

references.title: ACSM Position Stand: Progression models in resistance training for healthy adults
references.authors: American College of Sports Medicine (Ratamess NA et al.)
references.finding: Progressive resistance work, including bodyweight loading for novices, builds lower-body strength; squats are a foundational multi-joint pattern.

references.title: World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
references.authors: Bull FC, Al-Ansari SS, Biddle S, et al.
references.finding: Muscle-strengthening activity for all major muscle groups on 2+ days per week is a core recommendation for adults.

exercises.summary: The foundational lower-body strength move: sit the hips back and down, then drive back up through the whole foot.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Stand with feet shoulder width apart, toes turned out slightly. Send your hips back and down like sitting into a chair, keeping your chest up and heels heavy. Drive back up through your whole foot and squeeze your glutes at the top.

exercises.name: Push-up

references.title: The effects of a calisthenics training intervention on posture, strength and body composition
references.authors: Thomas E, Bianco A, Mancuso EP, Patti A, Tabacchi G, Paoli A, Messina G, Palma A
references.finding: Eight weeks of equipment-free calisthenics improved strength (including push-up performance), posture and body composition in untrained men.

references.title: ACSM Position Stand: Progression models in resistance training for healthy adults
references.authors: American College of Sports Medicine (Ratamess NA et al.)
references.finding: Multi-joint pressing with progressive overload builds upper-body pushing strength.

exercises.summary: Upper-body pressing staple for chest, shoulders and triceps, with the trunk working as a moving plank.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Start in a straight-arm plank with hands under your shoulders and body in one line. Lower your chest toward the floor with elbows about forty five degrees from your ribs. Press the floor away until your arms are straight. Drop to your knees any time to keep the line strong.
voiceFormCues: Elbows forty five degrees, not flared.

exercises.name: Forward lunge (alternating)

references.title: ACSM Position Stand: Progression models in resistance training for healthy adults
references.authors: American College of Sports Medicine (Ratamess NA et al.)
references.finding: Unilateral multi-joint lower-body work builds strength and balance with bodyweight loading appropriate for novices.

exercises.summary: Single-leg strength and balance: step forward, lower under control, push back to standing, alternate sides.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Step one foot forward and lower until both knees are near ninety degrees. Keep your torso tall and front heel heavy. Push through the front foot to step back together, then swap legs.

exercises.name: Reverse lunge (alternating)

references.title: ACSM Position Stand: Progression models in resistance training for healthy adults
references.authors: American College of Sports Medicine (Ratamess NA et al.)
references.finding: Unilateral lower-body patterns with bodyweight are effective strength stimuli; stepping backward reduces forward knee travel.

exercises.summary: A knee-friendlier lunge variation: step backward instead of forward, keeping the front shin more vertical.
exercises.voiceHowTo: From standing, step one foot straight back and bend both knees until the back knee hovers near the floor. Keep your weight in the front heel and torso upright. Drive through the front foot to return, then swap sides.

exercises.name: Forearm plank

references.title: The effects of a calisthenics training intervention on posture, strength and body composition
references.authors: Thomas E, Bianco A, Mancuso EP, Patti A, Tabacchi G, Paoli A, Messina G, Palma A
references.finding: Calisthenics programs including isometric trunk work improved posture and strength in untrained adults.

exercises.summary: Isometric trunk endurance: hold a straight line from head to heels on forearms and toes.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Set your elbows under your shoulders and step the feet back until your body is one straight line. Brace your belly like you are about to be poked, and squeeze your glutes. Breathe steadily and do not let the hips sag or pike.

exercises.name: Side plank

references.title: The effects of a calisthenics training intervention on posture, strength and body composition
references.authors: Thomas E, Bianco A, Mancuso EP, Patti A, Tabacchi G, Paoli A, Messina G, Palma A
references.finding: Isometric trunk holds are standard calisthenics elements shown to improve trunk strength and posture.

exercises.summary: Lateral trunk endurance: a straight-body hold on one forearm, hips lifted and stacked.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie on one side, elbow under your shoulder, feet stacked or staggered. Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line. Hold with your top hand on your hip or reaching to the ceiling, then switch sides halfway.
voiceFormCues: Push the floor away from the shoulder.

exercises.name: Glute bridge

references.title: ACSM Position Stand: Progression models in resistance training for healthy adults
references.authors: American College of Sports Medicine (Ratamess NA et al.)
references.finding: Hip-extension work is a recommended component of balanced resistance programs; the bridge is the standard low-load entry point.

exercises.summary: Hip-extension strength for glutes and hamstrings, gentle on knees and lower back.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, close to your hips. Press through your heels and lift the hips until your body lines up from shoulders to knees. Squeeze the glutes at the top, then lower with control.

exercises.name: Burpee

references.title: Effect of exercise intervention dosage on reducing visceral adipose tissue: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
references.authors: Chang YH, Yang HY, Shun SC
references.finding: HIIT produced the largest visceral fat reductions (SMD -0.39) and is effective even in sessions under 30 minutes.

references.title: Effect of High-Intensity Interval Training on Total, Abdominal and Visceral Fat Mass: A Meta-Analysis
references.authors: Maillard F, Pereira B, Boisseau N
references.finding: HIIT significantly reduces total, abdominal and visceral fat mass; whole-body weight-bearing intervals were most effective.

exercises.summary: Whole-body conditioning move: squat, kick to plank, return and jump. A HIIT staple with real visceral-fat evidence behind interval training.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Squat down and place your hands on the floor. Step or jump your feet back to a strong plank, then step or jump them back in. Stand and finish with a small jump, arms overhead. Move at a pace you can sustain for the whole interval.

exercises.name: Mountain climbers

references.title: Effect of exercise intervention dosage on reducing visceral adipose tissue: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
references.authors: Chang YH, Yang HY, Shun SC
references.finding: High-intensity interval work reduces visceral adipose tissue; mountain climbers are a standard HIIT movement.

exercises.summary: Plank-based cardio drive: knees run toward the chest while the trunk holds steady.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Start in a straight-arm plank with hands under shoulders. Drive one knee toward your chest, then switch legs in a running rhythm. Keep your hips low and shoulders over your wrists the whole time.

exercises.name: Jumping jacks

references.title: 2024 Adult Compendium of Physical Activities: A third update of the energy costs of human activities
references.authors: Herrmann SD, Willis EA, Ainsworth BE, et al.
references.journal: Journal of Sport and Health Science 13(1):6-12
references.finding: Vigorous calisthenics such as jumping jacks are catalogued at 7.5 METs — genuinely vigorous aerobic work.

references.title: World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
references.authors: Bull FC, Al-Ansari SS, Biddle S, et al.
references.finding: Vigorous-intensity aerobic activity counts double toward the weekly activity target.

exercises.summary: Classic whole-body vigorous cardio: jump feet wide while sweeping arms overhead, and back.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Stand tall with arms by your sides. Jump the feet wide while sweeping your arms overhead, then jump back together as the arms come down. Land softly on the balls of your feet with a steady rhythm.

exercises.name: High knees

references.title: Effect of exercise intervention dosage on reducing visceral adipose tissue: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
references.authors: Chang YH, Yang HY, Shun SC
references.finding: Vigorous aerobic intervals are among the most effective exercise modes for visceral fat reduction.

exercises.summary: Running on the spot with knees driving to hip height — vigorous, equipment-free cardio.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Run on the spot, driving each knee up toward hip height. Stay tall, land on the balls of your feet, and pump your arms like sprinting. Scale the height and speed to your fitness.

exercises.name: Squat jump

references.title: Effect of High-Intensity Interval Training on Total, Abdominal and Visceral Fat Mass: A Meta-Analysis
references.authors: Maillard F, Pereira B, Boisseau N
references.finding: Weight-bearing high-intensity intervals were the most effective HIIT mode for visceral fat loss.

exercises.summary: Explosive lower-body power: a full squat straight into a vertical jump with a soft landing.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Sit into a full squat, then drive up explosively and leave the ground. Land softly through the balls of your feet into the next squat. Rest a beat between reps if your landings get heavy.
voiceFormCues: Explode up, land like a cat.
Chest up out of the bottom.

exercises.name: Skater hops

references.title: 2024 Adult Compendium of Physical Activities: A third update of the energy costs of human activities
references.authors: Herrmann SD, Willis EA, Ainsworth BE, et al.
references.journal: Journal of Sport and Health Science 13(1):6-12
references.finding: Lateral bounding drills sit in the vigorous calisthenics band (~7 METs) — substantial aerobic demand with balance challenge.

exercises.summary: Side-to-side bounds landing on one leg — cardio plus lateral hip strength and balance.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Bound sideways from one foot to the other, swinging your arms across your body. Land softly on the outside leg with the knee bent, letting the trailing leg sweep behind. Keep your chest up and find a smooth skating rhythm.

exercises.name: Bird dog

references.title: The Effectiveness of Pilates Exercise in People with Chronic Low Back Pain: A Systematic Review
references.authors: Wells C, Kolt GS, Marshall P, Hill B, Bialocerkowski A
references.finding: Trunk-stability exercise programs reduce chronic low back pain; the bird dog is a standard quadruped stability drill in such programs.

exercises.summary: Quadruped trunk stability: opposite arm and leg reach while the spine stays quiet.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Start on hands and knees, wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your trunk. Pause, return with control, then switch sides without letting the hips rock.

exercises.name: Dead bug

references.title: The Effectiveness of Pilates Exercise in People with Chronic Low Back Pain: A Systematic Review
references.authors: Wells C, Kolt GS, Marshall P, Hill B, Bialocerkowski A
references.finding: Low-load trunk-control exercise is effective for back health; the dead bug trains anterior core control with the spine supported.

exercises.summary: Supine core control: lower opposite arm and leg while the lower back stays glued to the mat.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie on your back with arms to the ceiling and knees over hips at ninety degrees. Press your lower back into the mat, then lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor. Return and switch sides, moving only as far as your back stays flat.
voiceFormCues: Move slow, breathe out as you lower.

exercises.name: Superman hold

references.title: ACSM Position Stand: Progression models in resistance training for healthy adults
references.authors: American College of Sports Medicine (Ratamess NA et al.)
references.finding: Balanced programs include posterior-chain and spinal-erector work; prone extensions are the standard bodyweight option.

exercises.summary: Prone back-extension hold for spinal erectors and glutes.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie face down with arms extended overhead. Lift your chest, arms and legs a few centimetres off the floor and hold, gazing down to keep the neck long. Lower with control and repeat, or hold steadily for the interval.
voiceFormCues: Lift from the back, not the neck.

exercises.name: Wall sit

references.title: ACSM Position Stand: Progression models in resistance training for healthy adults
references.authors: American College of Sports Medicine (Ratamess NA et al.)
references.finding: Isometric holds develop muscular endurance; the wall sit is the classic bodyweight quadriceps isometric.

exercises.summary: Isometric quad endurance: back flat on the wall, thighs parallel to the floor, and hold.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Slide your back down a wall until your thighs are parallel to the floor and knees over ankles. Press your whole back into the wall and keep weight through your heels. Hold and breathe — hands off the thighs.

exercises.name: Inchworm walkout

references.title: The effects of a calisthenics training intervention on posture, strength and body composition
references.authors: Thomas E, Bianco A, Mancuso EP, Patti A, Tabacchi G, Paoli A, Messina G, Palma A
references.finding: Dynamic whole-body calisthenics movements improved strength and posture over eight weeks in untrained men.

exercises.summary: Fold, walk the hands out to a plank, walk back and stand — mobility plus core in one flow.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Fold forward and put your hands on the floor, bending knees as needed. Walk the hands out to a strong plank, pause, then walk them back and roll up to standing. Keep the core braced the whole way out and back.

exercises.name: Bear crawl

references.title: The effects of a calisthenics training intervention on posture, strength and body composition
references.authors: Thomas E, Bianco A, Mancuso EP, Patti A, Tabacchi G, Paoli A, Messina G, Palma A
references.finding: Whole-body crawling patterns fit the calisthenics model shown to improve strength and body composition.

exercises.summary: Crawling with knees hovering: shoulders, core and hips all working while you move on the spot.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Start on hands and knees, then hover the knees a few centimetres off the floor. Step the opposite hand and foot forward together, then the other pair — small controlled steps forward and back. Keep hips low and back flat like a table.

exercises.name: Crunch
exercises.popularityNote: Hugely popular as a 'belly fat burner', but controlled trials show abdominal exercise does not reduce abdominal fat — spot reduction is a myth. Crunches still train the rectus abdominis; just do not expect fat loss from them.

references.title: The effect of abdominal exercise on abdominal fat
references.authors: Vispute SS, Smith JD, LeCheminant JD, Hurley KS
references.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 25(9):2559-2564
references.finding: Six weeks of daily abdominal exercise produced no reduction in abdominal fat or girth versus control, despite improved endurance.

exercises.summary: Classic abdominal curl. Trains the abs; does not burn belly fat (see the evidence note).
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie on your back, knees bent, hands lightly behind your head. Curl your ribs toward your hips until the shoulder blades leave the mat, then lower slowly. Keep your chin off your chest and never yank the neck.
voiceFormCues: Curl the ribs, not the neck.

exercises.name: Russian twist
exercises.popularityNote: A social-media favourite for 'obliques and love handles'. Rotational endurance is real, but localized fat loss is not — regional training does not strip fat from the trained area.

references.title: Regional fat changes induced by localized muscle endurance resistance training
references.authors: Ramirez-Campillo R, Andrade DC, Campos-Jara C, Henriquez-Olguin C, Alvarez-Lepin C, Izquierdo M
references.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 27(8):2219-2224
references.finding: Twelve weeks of high-volume localized training reduced fat everywhere except the trained region — direct evidence against spot reduction.

exercises.summary: Seated trunk rotations. Fine oblique endurance work; no effect on waistline fat (see note).
exercises.voiceHowTo: Sit with knees bent and lean back until your abs switch on, spine long. Rotate your chest and hands to one side, then the other, letting your gaze follow your hands. Keep the movement in the trunk rather than just swinging the arms.

exercises.name: March in place

references.title: World Health Organization 2020 guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
references.authors: Bull FC, Al-Ansari SS, Biddle S, et al.
references.finding: Light-to-moderate aerobic movement counts toward activity targets and is the standard way to raise heart rate gradually before harder work.

exercises.summary: Gentle pulse-raiser to start a session: rhythmic marching with a relaxed arm swing.
exercises.voiceHowTo: March on the spot with a comfortable knee lift and easy arm swing. Grow the knee height and pace gradually as your body warms. Breathe easily — this should feel light.

exercises.name: Arm circles and reaches

references.title: ACSM Position Stand: Progression models in resistance training for healthy adults
references.authors: American College of Sports Medicine (Ratamess NA et al.)
references.finding: Dynamic range-of-motion work is the recommended pre-training preparation for the involved joints.

exercises.summary: Shoulder warm-up: big slow circles and overhead reaches to wake up the upper body.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Sweep both arms in big slow circles, forward for a while and then backward. Add tall overhead reaches, growing the range as the shoulders loosen. Keep the neck relaxed throughout.

exercises.name: Cat-cow

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Spinal mobility and flexibility work shows strong evidence for improving flexibility in healthy adults.

exercises.summary: Gentle spinal waves between arched and rounded positions — the standard back mobiliser.
exercises.voiceHowTo: On hands and knees, inhale as you drop the belly and lift your gaze — that is cow. Exhale as you round the spine to the ceiling and tuck the chin — that is cat. Flow slowly between the two with your breath.
voiceFormCues: Whole spine, not just the neck.

exercises.name: Seated hamstring stretch

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Regular flexibility training reliably improves range of motion in healthy adults.

exercises.summary: Cool-down staple: long spine reach over a straight leg to lengthen the hamstrings.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Sit tall with one leg long and the other foot tucked to your thigh. Hinge forward from the hips over the straight leg until you feel a comfortable stretch behind the thigh. Hold and breathe, then swap legs halfway.

exercises.name: Standing quad stretch

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Static stretching after training maintains and improves joint range of motion.

exercises.summary: Balance on one leg and draw the other heel to your glutes to release the front of the thigh.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Stand tall, catch one ankle behind you and draw the heel toward your glutes. Keep the knees close together and hips pushed slightly forward. Hold onto a wall if balance is shaky, and swap legs halfway.

exercises.name: Child's pose

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Gentle sustained stretching is an evidence-supported way to wind down and maintain flexibility.

exercises.summary: Resting fold: hips to heels, arms long, slow breathing to finish the session.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Kneel, sit your hips back toward your heels and walk your hands forward until your forehead rests down. Let the back broaden and breathe slowly into your ribs. Stay heavy and relaxed.

exercises.name: Footwork — heels

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Pilates shows strong evidence for flexibility and dynamic balance and moderate evidence for muscular endurance — footwork is the method's foundational leg-endurance series.

exercises.summary: The reformer's foundation: rhythmic leg presses with heels on the bar, hips quiet.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie on the carriage with heels hip-width on the foot bar and toes flexed back. Press the carriage out until your legs are long without locking the knees, then bend to return with control. Keep your pelvis heavy and still the whole time.

reformer.bodyPosition: lying supine on the carriage, heels on the foot bar

exercises.name: Footwork — toes

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Pilates leg-press patterns build muscular endurance; the toes variation adds calf and ankle work.

exercises.summary: Footwork with the balls of the feet on the bar — same press, extra calf and ankle work.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Place the balls of your feet on the bar with heels lifted and level. Press the carriage out long, keeping the heels still, then bend back in with control. Imagine your kneecaps tracking straight along rails.

reformer.bodyPosition: lying supine on the carriage, balls of the feet on the bar

exercises.name: Pelvic curl

references.title: Pilates for low back pain
references.authors: Yamato TP, Maher CG, Saragiotto BT, Hancock MJ, Ostelo RWJG, Cabral CMN, Menezes Costa LC, Costa LOP
references.finding: Pilates is probably more effective than minimal intervention for chronic low back pain; segmental bridging patterns are core to those programs.

references.title: The Effectiveness of Pilates Exercise in People with Chronic Low Back Pain: A Systematic Review
references.authors: Wells C, Kolt GS, Marshall P, Hill B, Bialocerkowski A
references.finding: Pilates programs significantly reduced chronic low back pain versus comparators in randomized trials.

exercises.summary: Segmental bridge on the carriage: roll the spine up and down one vertebra at a time.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie on the carriage with feet on the bar, knees bent. Exhale and roll your hips up one vertebra at a time until you form a line from shoulders to knees. Inhale at the top, then melt the spine back down from the chest to the tailbone.

reformer.bodyPosition: lying supine on the carriage, feet on the bar, knees bent

exercises.name: The hundred

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Moderate evidence that Pilates improves muscular endurance — the hundred is the method's signature endurance drill.

exercises.summary: Pilates' signature endurance drill: curled head and shoulders, legs in tabletop, arms pumping with the breath.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie back, curl your head and shoulders up and float the legs to tabletop. Reach your arms long by your hips and pump them briskly, breathing in for five pumps and out for five. Keep the lower back anchored the whole time.
voiceFormCues: In for five, out for five.

reformer.bodyPosition: lying supine on the carriage, head and shoulders curled, legs in tabletop

exercises.name: Leg circles in straps

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Strong evidence for flexibility gains from Pilates practice; supine leg circles mobilise the hips under light load.

exercises.summary: Hip mobility under light spring load: smooth controlled circles with legs in the straps.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lying on your back with feet in the straps, reach both legs to the ceiling. Draw slow circles the size of a dinner plate, keeping the pelvis perfectly still. Circle one way, then reverse at the halfway beep.

reformer.bodyPosition: lying supine on the carriage, feet in the straps

exercises.name: Frog

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Pilates strap work under light load builds hip mobility and inner-thigh control with the spine supported.

exercises.summary: In the straps: heels together, knees wide, press long and resist the return — inner thighs and hip control.
exercises.voiceHowTo: With feet in the straps, bring heels together and let the knees open wide. Press both legs out long on a low diagonal, then bend back in resisting the springs. Keep the tailbone heavy on the carriage throughout.

reformer.bodyPosition: lying supine on the carriage, feet in the straps, heels together knees wide

exercises.name: Elephant

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Pilates improves flexibility and trunk endurance; the elephant combines a hamstring stretch with abdominal control.

exercises.summary: Standing pike on the carriage: flat back, straight legs, small carriage pushes from the abdominals and hamstrings.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Stand on the carriage with hands on the foot bar, heels down and hips high in a pike. Keeping arms and legs long, press the carriage back a hand-width using your abdominals, then draw it home. Small moves, big control.

reformer.bodyPosition: standing on the carriage in a pike, hands on the foot bar

exercises.name: Knee stretches

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Moderate evidence for muscular endurance from Pilates; knee stretches are a classic abdominal-endurance drill with rhythm.

exercises.summary: Kneeling on the carriage, hands on the bar: rhythmic knee drives powered by the abdominals.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Kneel on the carriage with hands on the bar and hips over the knees, back gently rounded. Press the carriage back with your knees, then snap it home using your abdominals rather than momentum. Keep your shoulders quiet over the hands.

reformer.bodyPosition: kneeling on the carriage, hands on the foot bar

exercises.name: Long stretch

references.title: The Effectiveness of Pilates Exercise in People with Chronic Low Back Pain: A Systematic Review
references.authors: Wells C, Kolt GS, Marshall P, Hill B, Bialocerkowski A
references.finding: Trunk-stability training under load is central to effective Pilates programs; the long stretch is a moving plank demanding continuous trunk control.

exercises.summary: A moving plank: hands on the bar, feet against the shoulder rests, slide the whole line out and back.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Take a plank on the reformer with hands on the bar and feet against the shoulder rests. Keeping the body in one rigid line, press the carriage back through your shoulders, then return without the hips sagging. Think of sliding a plank of wood.

reformer.bodyPosition: plank on the reformer, hands on the bar, feet at the shoulder rests

exercises.name: Up stretch (pike)

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Pilates flow work develops trunk endurance and shoulder control; the up-stretch moves between pike and plank under spring load.

exercises.summary: Flowing between a high pike and a long plank, moving the carriage with control.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Start in a high pike with feet against the shoulder rests and hands on the bar. Lengthen your hips forward toward a plank as the carriage glides out, then lift the hips to pike as it returns. Keep the movement silky and continuous.

reformer.bodyPosition: pike on the reformer, hands on the bar, feet at the shoulder rests

exercises.name: Chest expansion

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Pilates improves posture-related muscular endurance; chest expansion targets the upper back and shoulder stabilisers.

exercises.summary: Kneeling tall, pull the straps to your hips and open the chest — posture and upper-back work.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Kneel tall on the carriage holding a strap in each hand, arms reaching forward. Pull both arms straight back beside your hips as the chest broadens, hold while you turn your head each way, then return slowly. Grow taller with every pull.

reformer.bodyPosition: kneeling tall on the carriage, facing the straps

exercises.name: Rowing from the chest

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Seated Pilates rowing sequences build upper-back endurance and trunk control under light spring load.

exercises.summary: Seated rowing with the straps: elbows drive back, trunk tall and unmoving.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Sit tall on the carriage facing the straps with legs crossed or long. Draw the elbows back low past your ribs, squeezing between the shoulder blades. Return with control, keeping your trunk perfectly upright throughout.

reformer.bodyPosition: seated tall on the carriage, facing the straps

exercises.name: Reformer lunge and hip stretch

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Strong evidence for flexibility improvements; the reformer lunge loads the hip-flexor stretch with gentle spring assistance.

exercises.summary: One foot down, one knee on the sliding carriage: a deep, supported hip-flexor opener.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Place one foot on the floor platform and the other knee on the carriage. Let the carriage glide back until you feel a deep stretch through the front of the trailing hip. Stay tall, breathe, and swap sides at the halfway cue.

reformer.bodyPosition: kneeling lunge, front foot on the platform, rear knee on the carriage

exercises.name: Mermaid

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Strong evidence for flexibility gains; the mermaid is the method's signature lateral-flexion stretch.

exercises.summary: Side-seated reach over the head as the carriage glides — a deep side-body stretch.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Sit sideways on the carriage with legs folded, one hand on the bar. Reach the free arm up and over your head as the carriage glides out, opening the whole side body. Use an inhale to lengthen, an exhale to return, then swap sides halfway.

reformer.bodyPosition: seated sideways on the carriage, legs folded, one hand on the bar

exercises.name: Feet in straps — press and lower

references.title: Pilates for low back pain
references.authors: Yamato TP, Maher CG, Saragiotto BT, Hancock MJ, Ostelo RWJG, Cabral CMN, Menezes Costa LC, Costa LOP
references.finding: Supported hip and hamstring work features in Pilates programs with probable benefit for chronic low back pain.

exercises.summary: Supine hamstring and hip work: legs press long and lower toward the bar against the springs.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lying on your back with feet in the straps, press both legs long toward the ceiling. Lower the legs toward the foot bar only as far as your lower back stays anchored, then float them back up. Move with slow, even breath.

reformer.bodyPosition: lying supine on the carriage, feet in the straps

exercises.name: Pulling straps (supine)

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: Strap pulling patterns train shoulder and upper-back endurance with the trunk stabilised.

exercises.summary: Lying down, sweep straight arms from the ceiling to your hips against the springs — lats and posture muscles.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie on your back holding a strap in each hand, arms reaching to the ceiling. Sweep both straight arms down to your sides until the hands hover by your hips, then return slowly. Keep the ribs heavy and the neck relaxed.

reformer.bodyPosition: lying supine on the carriage, one strap in each hand

exercises.name: Side splits (standing)
exercises.popularityNote: A studio favourite that looks spectacular on social media. Inner-thigh strength and balance demands are real, but there is no direct trial evidence for this exercise, and the moving carriage adds a slip risk — keep the range conservative.

references.title: A systematic review of the effects of Pilates method of exercise in healthy people
references.authors: Cruz-Ferreira A, Fernandes J, Laranjo L, Bernardo LM, Silva A
references.journal: Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation 92(12):2071-2081
references.finding: General Pilates evidence supports flexibility and balance outcomes, but individual advanced exercises like standing side splits lack direct study.

exercises.summary: Standing astride the carriage and platform, slide out and draw in — adductors and balance. Advanced; limited direct evidence.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Stand with one foot on the platform and the other on the carriage, toes forward. Let the carriage slide out to a comfortable straddle, then draw it home by squeezing the inner thighs. Keep your hips tall and hands reaching forward for balance.

reformer.bodyPosition: standing astride, one foot on the platform and one on the carriage

exercises.name: Warm-up flat

references.title: Health Benefits of Indoor Cycling: A Systematic Review
references.authors: Chavarrias M, Carlos-Vivas J, Collado-Mateo D, Perez-Gomez J
references.finding: Reviewed indoor cycling programs consistently open with 5-10 minutes of light-resistance riding to raise heart rate gradually.

exercises.summary: Easy seated spinning to wake the legs up. Remember the GR7 flywheel is fixed — keep the legs moving and slow down gradually.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Settle into the saddle with a light gear and spin at a comfortable eighty to ninety r p m. Relax your grip, soft elbows, eyes forward. Let the heart rate drift up gently — this bike has a fixed flywheel, so always keep the legs turning and slow down gradually.

exercises.name: Recovery spin

references.title: Exercise Intensity During Indoor Cycling (Intensidad de ejercicio en ciclismo indoor)
references.authors: Barbado C, Foster C, Vicente-Campos D, Lopez-Chicharro J
references.journal: Revista Internacional de Medicina y Ciencias de la Actividad Fisica y del Deporte 17(67)
references.finding: Indoor cycling classes routinely run above 90% HRmax; deliberate recovery segments are needed to keep sessions at sustainable intensity.

exercises.summary: Light-gear spinning between efforts — the deliberate recovery most classes skip.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Back the resistance right off and settle into an easy seated spin. Let your breathing come down and shake out one arm at a time. Stay smooth — recovery now buys quality in the next effort.

exercises.name: Seated flat — steady state

references.title: The Effect of Exercise on Visceral Adipose Tissue in Overweight Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
references.authors: Vissers D, Hens W, Taeymans J, Baeyens JP, Poortmans J, Van Gaal L
references.finding: Moderate-to-high intensity aerobic training has the highest potential to reduce visceral adipose tissue, even without dieting.

references.title: Health Benefits of Indoor Cycling: A Systematic Review
references.authors: Chavarrias M, Carlos-Vivas J, Collado-Mateo D, Perez-Gomez J
references.finding: Indoor cycling improves VO2max by around 8-10% and lowers blood pressure across reviewed trials.

exercises.summary: The bread-and-butter aerobic block: moderate gear, conversational-but-working pace.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Ride seated with a moderate gear at eighty five to ninety five r p m. You should be able to speak in short sentences but not sing. Keep the upper body quiet and let the legs do the talking.
voiceFormCues: Even pressure all the way round.

exercises.name: Fast flat — leg speed

references.title: Health Benefits of Indoor Cycling: A Systematic Review
references.authors: Chavarrias M, Carlos-Vivas J, Collado-Mateo D, Perez-Gomez J
references.finding: Higher-cadence aerobic work is a standard component of the indoor cycling programs shown to improve fitness.

exercises.summary: Cadence surge on a moderate gear — leg speed without going anaerobic. Keep resistance on; never spin against nothing.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Hold your moderate gear and lift the cadence toward one hundred r p m. Stay planted in the saddle with hips still — if you start bouncing, add a touch of resistance. Smooth fast circles.

exercises.name: Seated climb

references.title: The Effect of Exercise on Visceral Adipose Tissue in Overweight Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
references.authors: Vissers D, Hens W, Taeymans J, Baeyens JP, Poortmans J, Van Gaal L
references.finding: Moderate-to-high intensity aerobic work is the most effective exercise mode for visceral fat.

exercises.summary: Heavier gear, slower legs: the seated hill that builds leg strength and aerobic power together.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Add resistance until the legs slow to sixty to eighty r p m — the road is tilting up. Slide slightly back in the saddle and drive through the whole pedal stroke. Keep your breathing deep and rhythmic.

exercises.name: Heavy seated climb

references.title: Effect of exercise intervention dosage on reducing visceral adipose tissue: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
references.authors: Chang YH, Yang HY, Shun SC
references.finding: Higher-intensity aerobic work drives visceral fat loss; heavy climb segments push intensity while staying low impact.

exercises.summary: Near the top of the gear range: a grinding seated climb for strength-endurance.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Take the gear up again — this is the steep pitch. Keep the cadence at sixty to seventy r p m, hips anchored, and pull through the bottom of the stroke. If the legs stall, ease one level off.
voiceFormCues: Ease off one level if you stall.

exercises.name: Standing climb

references.title: Health Benefits of Indoor Cycling: A Systematic Review
references.authors: Chavarrias M, Carlos-Vivas J, Collado-Mateo D, Perez-Gomez J
references.finding: Mixed seated/standing indoor cycling programs improved fitness and body composition markers across trials.

exercises.summary: Out of the saddle on a heavy gear. Safety first: add resistance BEFORE you stand — the flywheel must support you.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Add solid resistance first, then rise out of the saddle with hands wide on the bars. Keep your weight centred over the pedals and let the bike rock gently beneath you. Legs turn at sixty to seventy five r p m — powerful, unhurried strokes.

exercises.name: Standing run

references.title: 2024 Adult Compendium of Physical Activities: A third update of the energy costs of human activities
references.authors: Herrmann SD, Willis EA, Ainsworth BE, et al.
references.journal: Journal of Sport and Health Science 13(1):6-12
references.finding: Spin-class style riding is catalogued at 9.0 METs — vigorous aerobic work.

exercises.summary: Running out of the saddle on a moderate gear — vigorous and rhythmic, hips over the pedals.
exercises.voiceHowTo: With a moderate gear, stand tall and run the pedals at around eighty to ninety r p m. Hips stay over the pedals, hands light on the bars. Find a bounce-free running rhythm you could hold for a song.

exercises.name: Jumps

references.title: Health Benefits of Indoor Cycling: A Systematic Review
references.authors: Chavarrias M, Carlos-Vivas J, Collado-Mateo D, Perez-Gomez J
references.finding: Position transitions are a standard element of the indoor cycling classes shown to improve fitness; jumps train smooth seated-to-standing control.

exercises.summary: Controlled transitions: four counts standing, four counts seated, on a supportive gear.
exercises.voiceHowTo: On a moderate-to-heavy gear, rise smoothly out of the saddle for four counts, then lower back with control for four. The legs keep turning evenly the whole time. Be comfortable with seated and standing riding before you play with jumps.
voiceFormCues: Up two three four, down two three four.

exercises.name: Sprint (30 seconds max)

references.title: The effects of high-intensity interval training vs. moderate-intensity continuous training on body composition in overweight and obese adults
references.authors: Wewege M, van den Berg R, Ward RE, Keech A
references.finding: Sprint-style interval training matches continuous training for fat loss in about 40% less time.

references.title: Aerobic high-intensity intervals improve VO2max more than moderate training
references.authors: Helgerud J, Hoydal K, Wang E, et al.
references.finding: High-intensity intervals produce superior aerobic fitness gains compared with work-matched moderate training.

exercises.summary: All-out effort in a high gear, capped at 30 seconds. Real resistance on — never sprint against a light flywheel.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Add gear so the flywheel has real bite, then go — an all-out effort at one hundred to one hundred ten r p m. Stay in control: strong core, still hips. Thirty seconds is the ceiling; empty the tank.

exercises.name: Tabata sprint (20 seconds)

references.title: Effects of moderate-intensity endurance and high-intensity intermittent training on anaerobic capacity and VO2max
references.authors: Tabata I, Nishimura K, Kouzaki M, Hirai Y, Ogita F, Miyachi M, Yamamoto K
references.finding: The original 20s:10s protocol improved both VO2max and anaerobic capacity in six weeks.

references.title: The Effect of Low-Volume High-Intensity Interval Training on Body Composition and Cardiorespiratory Fitness
references.authors: Sultana RN, Sabag A, Keating SE, Johnson NA
references.finding: Honest caveat: very-low-volume HIIT improves fitness but is not a shortcut for fat mass reduction on its own.

exercises.summary: The classic 20-on/10-off sprint. Superb for fitness; pair with bigger weekly volume for fat loss (see references).
exercises.voiceHowTo: Twenty seconds as hard as you can turn the gear, then ten seconds soft — that is one round. Keep the resistance meaningful so the flywheel never runs away from you. Hold your form even when it burns.
voiceFormCues: Form holds even when it burns.

exercises.name: Cool-down spin

references.title: Health Benefits of Indoor Cycling: A Systematic Review
references.authors: Chavarrias M, Carlos-Vivas J, Collado-Mateo D, Perez-Gomez J
references.finding: Reviewed class formats close with progressive cool-downs of easy spinning followed by stretching.

exercises.summary: Wind the gear and legs down gradually — remember the fixed flywheel keeps the pedals turning.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Take the resistance down low and let the legs slow gradually — never stop the pedals dead on this fixed flywheel. Breathe long and slow, letting the heart rate step down. Finish with the lever pressed to brake, then stretch off the bike.

exercises.name: Warm-up glide

references.title: Comparison of energy expenditure on a treadmill vs. an elliptical device at a self-selected exercise intensity
references.authors: Brown GA, Cook CM, Krueger RD, Heelan KA
references.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 24(6):1643-1649
references.finding: Elliptical training matches treadmill energy expenditure at matched effort — a low-impact way to warm into cardio work.

exercises.summary: Easy strides to grease the pattern and raise the pulse gently.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Start with a light level and long easy strides, hands resting on the moving handles. Let your heart rate climb gently over the first minutes. Stand tall — no slouching over the console.

elliptical.arms: light hold on the moving handles

exercises.name: Steady forward stride

references.title: The Effect of Exercise on Visceral Adipose Tissue in Overweight Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
references.authors: Vissers D, Hens W, Taeymans J, Baeyens JP, Poortmans J, Van Gaal L
references.finding: Moderate-intensity aerobic training reduces visceral fat — the steady elliptical block is the app's low-impact MICT workhorse.

references.title: Comparison of energy expenditure on a treadmill vs. an elliptical device at a self-selected exercise intensity
references.authors: Brown GA, Cook CM, Krueger RD, Heelan KA
references.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 24(6):1643-1649
references.finding: At matched effort the elliptical burns the same energy as a treadmill; note heart rate reads about 19 bpm higher, so go by feel.

exercises.summary: The moderate continuous block: mid resistance, purposeful stride, short-sentences effort.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Bring the level up to the middle of the range and stride with purpose, driving through the handles. Aim for an effort where short sentences are possible but singing is not. Shoulders back, whole foot on the pedal.

exercises.name: HIIT push

references.title: Effect of exercise intervention dosage on reducing visceral adipose tissue: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
references.authors: Chang YH, Yang HY, Shun SC
references.finding: HIIT produced the largest visceral fat reductions of any exercise mode (SMD -0.39).

references.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of interval training versus moderate-intensity continuous training on body adiposity
references.authors: Keating SE, Johnson NA, Mielke GI, Coombes JS
references.finding: Interval training is a time-efficient equivalent to continuous training for reducing body adiposity.

exercises.summary: Hard interval: high resistance and fast stride together. RPE 8 out of 10 — one-word answers only.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Punch the resistance up and drive — fast stride, hard pull and push through the handles. This is an eight out of ten effort where one-word answers are all you have. Hold your posture tall right to the end of the interval.

exercises.name: Easy recovery

references.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of interval training versus moderate-intensity continuous training on body adiposity
references.authors: Keating SE, Johnson NA, Mielke GI, Coombes JS
references.finding: Effective interval protocols alternate hard efforts with genuine low-intensity recovery periods.

exercises.summary: Drop resistance and stride rate until you can catch your breath — RPE 3 to 4.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Bring the level right down and soften the stride until your breath comes back. Light grip, loose shoulders. When you can speak easily again, you are ready for the next push.

exercises.name: Reverse stride

references.title: Comparison of energy expenditure on a treadmill vs. an elliptical device at a self-selected exercise intensity
references.authors: Brown GA, Cook CM, Krueger RD, Heelan KA
references.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 24(6):1643-1649
references.finding: Elliptical work delivers treadmill-level energy expenditure at low impact; direction changes vary the stimulus. EMG data show backward striding mainly raises quad (rectus femoris) activity.

exercises.summary: Pedal backwards for a quad-emphasis change of stimulus. Hands on the static rail for balance.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Slow down, then smoothly reverse the pedal direction. Sit slightly back into your hips and feel the front of the thighs take over. Keep your hands on the static rail until the backward rhythm feels stable.

elliptical.arms: hands on the static rail for balance

exercises.name: Legs only — no handles

references.title: Comparison of energy expenditure on a treadmill vs. an elliptical device at a self-selected exercise intensity
references.authors: Brown GA, Cook CM, Krueger RD, Heelan KA
references.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 24(6):1643-1649
references.finding: Elliptical training is an effective treadmill alternative; removing the arm drive shifts the workload to the legs and balance system (coaching convention — direct EMG evidence is limited).

exercises.summary: Let go of the moving handles: legs and core carry the whole stride.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Rest your hands on the static rail — or hover them — and keep the stride going with legs alone. Feel the core switch on to keep you steady. Hold your stride rate even though the arms are on holiday.

elliptical.arms: legs only, hands resting on the static rail

exercises.name: Arms emphasis drive

references.title: Comparison of energy expenditure on a treadmill vs. an elliptical device at a self-selected exercise intensity
references.authors: Brown GA, Cook CM, Krueger RD, Heelan KA
references.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 24(6):1643-1649
references.finding: Whole-body elliptical work raises total energy demand; emphasising the handle drive engages the upper body (coaching convention — direct EMG evidence is limited).

exercises.summary: Push and pull hard through the moving handles — share the work with your upper body.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Grip the moving handles and make the arms genuine partners — push away strongly and pull back with intent. Let the legs keep an even rhythm while the upper body raises the total workload. Keep the shoulders down away from the ears.

elliptical.arms: push and pull hard through the handles

exercises.name: Hill grind

references.title: The Effect of Exercise on Visceral Adipose Tissue in Overweight Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
references.authors: Vissers D, Hens W, Taeymans J, Baeyens JP, Poortmans J, Van Gaal L
references.finding: Higher-intensity aerobic work maximises visceral fat reduction; heavy-resistance elliptical blocks push intensity without impact.

exercises.summary: High resistance, slow powerful strides — the elliptical's answer to a standing climb.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Take the level high and let the stride slow into strong deliberate pushes. Drive through the heels and pull the handles with purpose — this is your hill. Keep breathing deep and rhythmic all the way up.

exercises.name: Cool-down glide

references.title: Comparison of energy expenditure on a treadmill vs. an elliptical device at a self-selected exercise intensity
references.authors: Brown GA, Cook CM, Krueger RD, Heelan KA
references.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research 24(6):1643-1649
references.finding: Progressive intensity reduction on the elliptical brings heart rate down while keeping movement low impact.

exercises.summary: Ease the level and stride down step by step until breathing is easy.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Step the resistance down low and let the stride soften. Breathe long and slow, unclench the hands, and let the heart rate walk back down. Finish feeling looser than you started.

elliptical.arms: light hold on the moving handles

exercises.name: McGill curl-up

references.title: Low back stability: from formal description to issues for performance and rehabilitation
references.authors: McGill SM
references.finding: Stabilization training should challenge the trunk while minimizing spine load — the basis of the curl-up / side bridge / bird dog 'big three'.

references.title: Exercise therapy for chronic low back pain
references.authors: Hayden JA, Ellis J, Ogilvie R, Malmivaara A, van Tulder MW
references.finding: Across 249 trials, exercise probably reduces pain and improves function in chronic low back pain (moderate-certainty evidence).

exercises.summary: The physio-designed abdominal exercise: a tiny head-and-shoulder lift with the spine held neutral — trains the abs without bending the lower back.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie on your back with one knee bent and the other leg long, hands resting under the arch of your lower back. Lift just your head and shoulders a few centimetres, as if they were on a tray, without flattening or arching the spine. Hold for ten seconds, breathe, and lower with control. Swap the bent leg halfway.
voiceFormCues: Spine stays neutral over your hands.

exercises.name: Side bridge (from knees)

references.title: Low back stability: from formal description to issues for performance and rehabilitation
references.authors: McGill SM
references.finding: The side bridge loads the lateral trunk stabilizers (quadratus lumborum, obliques) with one of the lowest spine-compression costs of any core exercise.

references.title: An update of stabilisation exercises for low back pain: a systematic review with meta-analysis
references.authors: Smith BE, Littlewood C, May S
references.finding: Stabilisation exercise benefits low back pain, comparably to other active exercise forms.

exercises.summary: McGill big-three lateral hold, scaled from the knees so it stays pain-safe while the side of the trunk works.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie on your side with knees bent back at ninety degrees and your elbow under your shoulder. Lift the hips forward and up until your body is straight from knees to head, and hold. Keep breathing, then lower softly. Swap sides at the halfway cue.

exercises.name: Bird dog (back care)

references.title: Low back stability: from formal description to issues for performance and rehabilitation
references.authors: McGill SM
references.finding: The bird dog trains back extensors and rotational stiffness with very low spine load — the third of the 'big three'.

references.title: Motor control exercise for chronic non-specific low-back pain
references.authors: Saragiotto BT, Maher CG, Yamato TP, Costa LOP, Menezes Costa LC, Ostelo RWJG, Macedo LG
references.finding: Motor control exercise is more effective than minimal intervention for chronic non-specific low back pain.

exercises.summary: Quadruped opposite-arm-and-leg reach with a stopwatch-steady spine — the classic back-safe extensor drill.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Start on hands and knees with a neutral spine. Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level, without letting the hips tip. Hold a slow breath, sweep them back under you, and switch sides. Imagine balancing a cup of tea on your lower back.

exercises.name: Dead bug (back care)

references.title: Motor control exercise for chronic non-specific low-back pain
references.authors: Saragiotto BT, Maher CG, Yamato TP, Costa LOP, Menezes Costa LC, Ostelo RWJG, Macedo LG
references.finding: Motor control training of deep trunk muscles reduces chronic low back pain versus minimal intervention.

exercises.summary: Anterior core control with the spine fully supported — the safest way to train the deep abdominals.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie on your back, arms to the ceiling, knees stacked over hips. Press the lower back gently into the mat, then lower one arm and the opposite leg only as far as the back stays glued down. Return and switch sides, slow and smooth.

exercises.name: Glute bridge (back care)

references.title: Exercise interventions for the treatment of chronic low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
references.authors: Searle A, Spink M, Ho A, Chuter V
references.finding: Strength/resistance and coordination/stabilisation programs are the most effective exercise types for chronic low back pain.

references.title: Which exercises target the gluteal muscles while minimizing activation of the tensor fascia lata? Electromyographic assessment using fine-wire electrodes
references.authors: Selkowitz DM, Beneck GJ, Powers CM
references.journal: Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy 43(2):54-64
references.finding: Bridging is among the best exercises for activating the gluteals selectively — strong hips take load off the lower back.

exercises.summary: Hip extension powered by the glutes, teaching the hips — not the lower back — to do the lifting.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat near your hips. Squeeze your glutes first, then lift the hips until shoulders, hips and knees line up — no arching past that point. Pause at the top and melt back down slowly.

exercises.name: Pelvic tilt

references.title: Motor control exercise for chronic non-specific low-back pain
references.authors: Saragiotto BT, Maher CG, Yamato TP, Costa LOP, Menezes Costa LC, Ostelo RWJG, Macedo LG
references.finding: Gentle motor-control drills that teach pelvic and deep-abdominal awareness are a core ingredient of effective programs.

exercises.summary: The entry-level physio drill: tiny rocking of the pelvis that wakes up the deep core and eases a stiff lower back.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. Gently flatten your lower back into the mat by rolling the pelvis, hold a moment, then release to neutral. Small, slow, and completely pain-free — this is a conversation with your spine, not a workout for it.
voiceFormCues: Roll the pelvis, ribs stay quiet.

exercises.name: Cat-cow (back care)

references.title: A Systematic Review of the Effects of Exercise and Physical Activity on Non-Specific Chronic Low Back Pain
references.authors: Gordon R, Bloxham S
references.finding: Programs combining strengthening with flexibility work are effective for non-specific chronic low back pain.

exercises.summary: Slow spinal waves through the whole back — mobility between the strength drills.
exercises.voiceHowTo: On hands and knees, inhale as the belly drops and the gaze lifts, then exhale as you round the spine to the ceiling and tuck the chin. Move through a comfortable range only, letting each breath set the pace. Think of moving one vertebra at a time.

exercises.name: Press-up (McKenzie extension)

references.title: The McKenzie method for low back pain: a systematic review of the literature with a meta-analysis approach
references.authors: Machado LA, de Souza MvS, Ferreira PH, Ferreira ML
references.finding: McKenzie extension work shows some benefit over passive therapy for acute low back pain; effects are modest — an honest MODERATE.

exercises.summary: The classic physio extension: press the chest up while the hips stay heavy, restoring comfortable backward bend.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie face down with hands under your shoulders. Press your chest up and forward while the hips and legs stay completely relaxed on the mat. Rise only as far as feels easy, exhale at the top, and lower slowly. If anything travels down a leg, stop and skip this one.
voiceFormCues: Stop if anything runs down a leg.

exercises.name: Hip hinge drill

references.title: Exercise interventions for the treatment of chronic low back pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
references.authors: Searle A, Spink M, Ho A, Chuter V
references.finding: Strength and coordination training are the most effective exercise approaches for chronic low back pain — the hinge is the coordination pattern behind every safe lift.

exercises.summary: Learning to bow from the hips with a proud flat back — the movement skill that protects your spine every time you pick something up.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Stand tall with soft knees and hands sliding down the front of your thighs. Push your hips straight back and let your flat chest tip forward like a drawbridge, stopping when the hamstrings tighten. Drive the hips forward to stand, squeezing the glutes at the top.

exercises.name: Clamshell

references.title: Which exercises target the gluteal muscles while minimizing activation of the tensor fascia lata? Electromyographic assessment using fine-wire electrodes
references.authors: Selkowitz DM, Beneck GJ, Powers CM
references.journal: Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy 43(2):54-64
references.finding: Fine-wire EMG showed the clam best activates the gluteals while minimizing tensor fascia lata activation — a physio staple for hip control.

exercises.summary: Side-lying knee opening that strengthens the deep hip stabilisers supporting the pelvis and lower back.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie on your side with hips and knees folded, feet together, head resting on your arm. Keeping the feet touching, float the top knee open like a clam shell, without rolling the pelvis back. Lower with control and keep a steady rhythm. Swap sides at the halfway cue.

exercises.name: Full side bridge

references.title: An update of stabilisation exercises for low back pain: a systematic review with meta-analysis
references.authors: Smith BE, Littlewood C, May S
references.finding: Stabilisation exercise improves low back pain; progressions keep the stimulus growing as tolerance builds.

exercises.summary: The straight-leg progression of the side bridge — earn it after the knee version feels easy.
exercises.voiceHowTo: From your side with legs long and feet stacked, set the elbow under the shoulder and lift the hips until you form one straight line. Hold with steady breathing and level hips. Drop back to the knee version any time form fades. Swap sides halfway.

exercises.name: Back extension hold

references.title: A review of the specificity of exercises designed for conditioning the lumbar extensors
references.authors: Steele J, Bruce-Low S, Smith D
references.finding: Honest caveat: free-body trunk extensions condition the whole posterior chain but poorly isolate the lumbar extensors — still useful, just not magic.

references.title: Best Exercise Options for Reducing Pain and Disability in Adults With Chronic Low Back Pain: Pilates, Strength, Core-Based, and Mind-Body. A Network Meta-analysis
references.authors: Fernandez-Rodriguez R, Alvarez-Bueno C, Cavero-Redondo I, Torres-Costoso A, Pozuelo-Carrascosa DP, Reina-Gutierrez S, Pascual-Morena C, Martinez-Vizcaino V
references.journal: Journal of Orthopaedic & Sports Physical Therapy 52(8):505-521
references.finding: Network meta-analysis of 118 RCTs: Pilates, strength, and core-based exercise are the most effective options for chronic low back pain.

exercises.summary: A gentle prone hold for the whole posterior chain — chest floats, legs stay grounded, effort stays mild.
exercises.voiceHowTo: Lie face down with arms beside you or swept slightly back. Float your chest a few centimetres off the mat, keeping the feet down and the neck long. Hold for a few steady breaths at a gentle effort, then lower softly.

exercises.name: Seated toe reach
exercises.popularityNote: Toe-touch stretching is hugely popular for a 'tight lower back', but the evidence that flexion stretching helps back pain is limited, and repeated loaded flexion can aggravate a sensitive spine. If it feels good, keep it gentle and seated; if your back is flared up, skip it and do pelvic tilts instead.

references.title: A Systematic Review of the Effects of Exercise and Physical Activity on Non-Specific Chronic Low Back Pain
references.authors: Gordon R, Bloxham S
references.finding: Flexibility work is supported only as part of a combined program — not as a stand-alone fix for back pain.

exercises.summary: The popular hamstring-and-back reach, kept seated and gentle. Real evidence for it is limited (see note).
exercises.voiceHowTo: Sit with one leg long and the other foot tucked in. Hinge gently forward over the straight leg, reaching toward the shin or toes, and stop well short of any pinch in the back. Breathe and let the stretch stay in the back of the thigh. Swap legs at the halfway cue.
voiceFormCues: Stretch lives in the thigh, not the spine.

routines.name: Pyramid Climb
routines.summary: Resistance ladders up to a standing-climb peak, then steps back down — the classic pyramid class shape.

routines.name: Tabata Sprints
routines.summary: Two Tabata blocks of 8 x 20s all-out / 10s soft, separated by a proper recovery spin.

routines.name: Rolling Hills
routines.summary: Three rolling climbs: seated build, standing crest, flat descent — repeat.

routines.name: Endurance Ride
routines.summary: Long steady aerobic blocks with one leg-speed surge — the MICT workhorse ride.

routines.name: 30/30 Sprint Intervals
routines.summary: Ten rounds of 30 seconds hard against 30 seconds soft — a classic 1:1 interval set.

routines.name: Climb Ladder
routines.summary: Step the resistance up stage by stage to a standing summit, then a run home.

routines.name: Jumps and Runs
routines.summary: Position-change playground: jump blocks and standing runs with honest recoveries.

routines.name: Resistance Pyramid
routines.summary: Resistance steps up to a hill-grind peak and back down, arms working on the shoulders of the pyramid.

routines.name: HIIT Intervals
routines.summary: Eight hard pushes with generous easy recoveries — the ACE-style elliptical HIIT shape.

routines.name: Direction Mix
routines.summary: Forward and reverse blocks with a legs-only balance challenge in the middle.

routines.name: Steady Cruise
routines.summary: The long moderate continuous session — 30 minutes of honest MICT with small texture changes.

routines.name: Arms and Legs Focus
routines.summary: Alternating arm-drive and legs-only blocks — upper body and balance take turns.
